Bhaktapur - Kathmandu Valley - Nepal

A Living Sense Of Place

An 18-room heritage boutique hotel in the medieval city of Bhaktapur, built around courtyards, Newari craft, and the five elements - two minutes on foot from Durbar Square.

18 Rooms and Suites 2 min to Durbar Square 4.9 Guest Rating

The Hotel

Where time slows

Bhaktapur is called the Museum of Life, and The Nanee is built in its image. The preserved brick lanes, carved windows, and temple squares of this ancient Newar city sit in quiet harmony with a hotel shaped by the same hands and materials - brick, wood, brass, and terracotta, gathered around open courtyards.

Inspired by the Nyatapola Temple and guided by Vaastu Shastra, every space is aligned to the five elements of nature, so the building itself feels balanced from the moment you step inside.

Vaastu Shastra

A sanctuary of quiet craft

With just eighteen rooms and suites, every gesture of hospitality stays personal. The design follows the five elements - earth, water, fire, air, and space - and each one has a place in the house. Choose an element to see where you will meet it.

Element 01 - Prithvi

Grounded in brick and clay

Bhaktapur is built from the earth it stands on. At The Nanee, terracotta, exposed brick, hand-thrown pottery, and woven basketry carry that grounding into every room, steady and warm under hand and foot.

Find it in - The Prithvi rooms, the pottery and terracotta throughout

Dine

Refined courtyard dining

Dining at The Nanee follows the rhythm of the seasons and the farms around Bhaktapur. Four spaces, four moods - from street food cooked over a traditional stove to dinner under the rooftop sky. Tap a space to read more.

Bara Shop

Street food, kept traditional

Authentic Newari street food in a traditional setting - Chuya Lah, Bara, and Samay Baji, cooked the slow way over a chulha stove.

Experiences

Taste it, do not just see it

At The Nanee, culture is something you take part in. Cook it, taste it course by course, and hear the stories that travel with each dish.

Hands On - With local cooks, at the hotel

Traditional Newari Cooking

A hands-on cooking class in traditional dishes, with the cultural stories behind them told as you work. You leave with recipes and a fuller sense of what Newari food means here.

Six Courses - Local pairings

Contemporary Newari Tasting Menu

A modern six-course reading of heritage recipes, paired with local drinks and told through immersive storytelling. Old flavours, handled with contemporary craft.

The Rooftop, After Dark - Six to ten courses

Exotic Chef's Table

Six to ten courses on the rooftop, blending Nepali and Newari cuisine with the stories of the people who cook it. High mountain organic teas and specialty Nepali coffee close the evening.

Baakha Kuthu - The Storytelling Room

Stories are how Bhaktapur remembers

Through Shruti Parampara, the tradition of passing history by word of mouth, local artisans, storytellers, and cultural experts come to The Nanee to share the narratives of the city - its monuments, its rituals, its people. Sit in, listen, and the squares outside start to read like a book you already know.

Concierge

Your personal guide to the city

The Nanee keeps an in-house culture expert, and the whole team takes an artisan's approach to your time. Temple bells at dawn, potters at work by mid-morning, a quiet courtyard lunch - your days here are shaped around the city's real rhythm, not a checklist.

Morning experienceA complimentary guided walk into Bhaktapur's early rituals and traditions, before the day crowds arrive.
Culture expertAn in-house guide to Newari heritage, on hand to deepen every walk and answer every question.
Day tripsPatan, Kathmandu, Nagarkot, and Dhulikhel are each 30 to 45 minutes away - the hotel is a calm base for the whole valley.
